items.title: More than 8 million Australians now receive income support
items.description: The number of people accessing income support payments has risen by 2 million in the past decade, with more Australians unable to work due to deteriorating mental and physical health.

items.title: 'Straw that broke the camel's back': Financial distress grows as rates rise
items.description: Almost 14,000 Australians rang the National Debt Helpline last month, with most callers saying they are struggling to pay their home loans and are facing mortgage stress, according to new data.

items.title: 'We're still here. We still have no idea': RBA warns of harsh Iran war reality
items.description: Australia had an inflation problem before the Iran war, but it's turned sinister. We've become hostage to oil prices, and as the governor of the Reserve Bank puts it: "We are all feeling poorer".

items.title: Labor axes funding for $45b Inland Rail project linking Melbourne to Brisbane
items.description: The federal government has halted plans for the Melbourne to Brisbane Inland Rail, amid concerns the project could cost more than $45 billion to complete.

items.title: Live: Rubio says 'Operation Epic Fury' concluded but with conditions
items.description: The United Arab Emirates has defended itself against more strikes, as the US tries to clear safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz. Follow live.

items.title: Kumanjayi Little Baby's family feel let down after missing court hearing
items.description: The family of a five-year-old girl who died after going missing from an Alice Springs town camp last month say they feel let down by the system after missing her alleged killer's first court date.

items.title: EV tax discount removed two days' worth of carbon emissions
items.description: Two days' worth of carbon emissions were removed thanks to the $2 billion electric vehicle tax discount. But its supporters say that put 64,000 more EVs on the road, jump-starting the struggling industry.

items.title: Negative gearing, capital gains tax and trusts explained simply
items.description: The government is poised to make changes to negative gearing, the capital gains tax discount, and the tax treatment of trusts in next week's federal budget. So how do they work, and what could the changes look like?

items.title: Live: Chalmers says fuel security package to be unveiled following National Cabinet meeting
items.description: Treasurer Jim Chalmers says a fuel security package will be unveiled following today's meeting of National Cabinet. Follow live.

items.title: Fuel price rises in Australia slow as costs soar in the US. Here's why
items.description: Fuel prices in Australia have started to moderate just as costs have reached an almost four-year high in the United States.

items.title: Will Donald Trump's 'Project Freedom' restart shipping or reignite war?
items.description: The US president is pledging to secure shipping through the jammed Strait of Hormuz. But "Project Freedom" is a risky exercise that threatens to shatter a shaky ceasefire.

items.title: The graphs that explain Farrer's by-election on Saturday
items.description: The first electoral test for both new coalition party leaders, Angus Taylor and Matt Canavan, sees the opposition at serious risk of losing Farrer for the first time since the seat was created in 1949.

items.title: Live: ASX to rise following gains on Wall St
items.description: The ASX is set to open higher following fresh records on two of Wall Street's major stock exchanges. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: How a flamboyant thief quietly pulled off an extraordinary coin heist
items.description: David Gee pulled off one of the most baroque and ambitious coin heists in Australian history, nicking precious coins from the special collections of the nation's oldest library without anybody noticing.

items.title: Phone books are still being delivered but does anyone use them?
items.description: Once a must-have household item, are phone books destined to go the way of the answering machine and rotary dial phone?

items.title: Quiz: Fancy yourself a jetsetter? Test your knowledge
items.description: Which country does the alcoholic spirit cachaça hail from? And how much do you know about Australian towns with Big Koala statues?

items.title: 'Australia's first attractive comedian' has never been in love
items.description: Last year, Elouise Eftos became the first Australian woman to land a best newcomer nod at Edinburgh Fringe. Now, she's got a new show about never falling in love.

items.title: 'Gut-wrenching' struggle for Australian designers finding copies on Shein
items.description: Small Australian fashion designers say it is too time-consuming to continue to ask Shein to take down copies of their designs.

items.title: Human-to-human transmission suspected in deadly hantavirus outbreak
items.description: The World Health Organization says no rats have been found on board the cruise vessel where the outbreak has taken hold, with three people having died of confirmed or suspected infections of the rodent-borne virus.

items.title: Man charged with manslaughter, drug driving over Woodford crash
items.description: Police charge a 31-year-old Brisbane man with manslaughter following a fatal crash allegedly involving a stolen utility at Woodford.

items.title: Big new hotel announced for Adelaide but are there enough already?
items.description: The latest major hotel project announced for Adelaide adds to a looming accommodation construction boom in the CBD.

items.title: Indigenous commissioner condemns comedian's 'deeply offensive' video
items.description: South Australia's Commissioner for Aboriginal Children and Young People speaks out against a "deeply offensive" social media video posted by comedian Alex "Shooter" Williamson in the wake of the death of Kumanjayi Little Baby.

items.title: Diverse communities 'absolutely scared' by NDIS cuts
items.description: Nidhi Shekaran is one of thousands of NDIS participants waiting to learn if their services will be impacted as part of sweeping government reforms to the scheme.

items.title: Medicines regulator urged to recall controversial cold and flu herb
items.description: Andrographis paniculata is a common ingredient in cold and flu supplements, but it may not be as low-risk as first thought.

items.title: The most important number isn't listed in Victoria's budget pages
items.description: The most important number in the Victorian budget isn't listed in its pages. It's the 206 days until the polls, with the Labor Government seeking an unprecedented fourth term.
